text:
kai: Heads-up — noticed a throughput drop on multi-node TPU-like jobs when we route to EFA region. p99 tokens/sec down ~18% compared to NVLink-only runs. Looks like all-reduce overhead + KV cache churn. Anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

maria: Yep saw something similar on the 2/24 nightly. Synthetic membench showed higher PCIe transaction stall time when we slice batches small. Might be kernel selection picking a fallback matmul for small seq lengths.

aj: Can you paste the perf log? I want to see if it's comm overlap or compute stall.

kai: Pasting clipped trace from the profiler (reduced):

```
# timeline: node0->node1 cross-node (EFA)
00:00.000 compute start
00:00.020 allreduce start (small-msg, 64KB chunks)
00:00.045 allreduce end
00:00.047 compute resume (KV cache miss path)
00:00.130 batch finish
# observed: many small allreduce windows; CPU+DMA busy; NVLink runs had fewer, larger windows
p50_latency: 120ms p95: 320ms p99: 640ms
```

zara: Interesting — NVLink runs aggregated into fewer larger allreduce ops (chunked 4MB), EFA path had 64KB chunking because topology sampler decided to minimize single-op size. That increases per-op latency and prevents compute overlap.

aj: If we see many small allreduces we pay setup overhead per-op on InfiniBand. Two levers: increase chunk size / reduce slice count, or prefer hierarchical allreduce with intra-node NVLink then inter-node EFA.

maria: Also saw KV cache invalidations correlating with batch slicing. When batch_slice changes between microbatches we drop some prefix entries and trigger recompute on resume. That explains the mid-batch compute stalls after comms.

kai: Repro steps I used: run this config on 4xA100 (2 nodes):

```
./run_infer --model redwood-7b --tp 2 --pp 2 --batch_size 8 --slice_size 128 --comm_strategy auto --fabric efa
```

and then run the same with --fabric nvlink (single node) and --slice_size 512. The latter had 15% better throughput.

aj: Can you run perf counters? I want cycles and PCIe stalls.

kai: Ran quick perf:

```
perf stat -e cycles,stalled-cycles-frontend,stalled-cycles-backend,cache-misses -p $PID -- sleep 30
# summary:
cycles: 3.2G
stalled-cycles-backend: 620M
cache-misses: 1.1M
# on EFA runs stalled cycles higher by ~25% vs NVLink
```

zara: That maps to DMA setup churn on the NIC side + small-message overhead. Proposed change: new kernel selector rule to prefer large-chunk allreduce when fabric == efa and node_count > 1, and bump default allreduce_chunk_bytes from 64KB -> 1MB for distributed path. Also add heuristic: if batch_slice < 256 tokens, coalesce two slices before issuing inter-node comms.

maria: I worry about tail latency if we push chunk size too high for tiny models. Maybe make chunk size adaptive: sample first 3 steps, if p95_allreduce_setup_time > threshold, increase chunk size.

aj: Agreed. We can implement a sampling probe in the scheduler: send a synthetic small-reduction for first microbatch and measure setup latency, then pick chunking strategy. Cheap and runtime-local.

kai: I put up a spike PR implementing the adaptive chunker + a new kernel preference for short-seq fused matmul (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5123). It toggles kernel to favor fused-fp16 paths for seq_len <= 128 on GPU to avoid fallback to generic kernel.

zara: Nice. Did you run canaries?

kai: Canary run on staging (4 nodes) started at 1969987690. Results: throughput +8% for efa path, p99 latency improved ~6%. No regressions on NVLink baseline.

canary-bot: Canary deployment 1969987690 -> canary-group-efa: pass (success). Metrics: throughput +7.8%, p99 latency -6.1%, error rate unchanged.

maria: Do we have perf traces from the canary so we can compare before/after pprof stacks?

kai: Attached condensed flame (inline excerpt):

```
# before: lots of small allreduce windows, kernel fallback at matmul_generic
# after: intra-node reduce -> inter-node larger ops, kernel fused_matmul_fp16 hit rate +42%
# net: less backend-stall, fewer cache invalidations mid-batch
```

aj: Two follow-ups: 1) add a KV-cache conservatism flag that disables aggressive cache eviction when we detect high inter-node comms, 2) instrument kernel selector to emit reasons in traces so we can audit when it picks fallback kernels.

zara: I filed infra tickets: INF-945 (adaptive-chunker rollout), INF-946 (kernel-selector trace labels), INF-947 (kv-conservatism flag).

maria: For rollout plan — keep canary on efa-only customers for 48h, monitor token-per-second and p99. If stable, flip for multi-node customers. Also add an automated rollback if p99 increases by >10% in 15m.

kai: I'll queue follow-up PR to add the probe and the conservative-kv flag. Will also add a small-unit microbench for chunk sizes (scripts/eval/chunk_probe.py).

aj: One more note: for heterogeneous racks where some machines have NVLink and others only PCIe, prefer hierarchical allreduce by default. We should route intra-node via nvlink topology map at the runtime level rather than relying on the cluster manager. I'll sketch a topology-aware planner.

zara: Good call. That planner can reuse the existing topology graph from infra-agent. I'll add a small API to expose local interconnect speeds.

kai: Thanks team. Summary action items: implement adaptive chunk probe (kai), kernel-selector trace labels (aj), kv-conservatism flag (maria), add topology-aware planner stub (zara). I'll monitor the 48h canary and post results. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INF-945 assigned to kai, INF-946 assigned to aj, INF-947 assigned to maria. Due: 2026-01-15.

zara: Also annotate the PR with perf artifacts and the microbench so SRE can run load tests.

kai: Will do. If anyone wants to reproduce locally use the run_infer command and the chunk_probe script I just added to the PR.

maria: Thanks — this explains the weird mid-batch stalls we saw in customer X's Dedicated cluster. Good find.

aj: Cool, closing loop once infra tickets show green.
